featured_reviews.review_text:
Wish I could give her negative stars—not even a zero would be enough.

My brother had a fungal infection and was already consulting another doctor, but I wasn't comfortable with a male doctor, so I decided to consult a lady doctor. It turns out, my brother’s doctor is her husband, and he referred me to Dr. Varsha Pandey.

She took one look at my infection and didn’t ask me any further questions—not about my symptoms, medical history, or anything else. She didn’t explain what the condition was or how the treatment would work. She simply prescribed some medicines and told me to take an injection every alternate day for a month, each costing ₹200. My brother had been taking the same injections for ₹100, which immediately raised doubts in my mind.

She spent barely two minutes with me before asking me to wait outside. Then her assistant came out with the prescription and explained the medications. The assistant seemed like a child—I seriously doubt she was even qualified for the job she was doing.

Finally, I was asked to pay ₹1,100. I added up the cost of the medicines, which totaled around ₹500. I asked what the rest was for, and she casually said ₹250 was the consultation fee. I pointed out that even then, the math didn’t add up.

When I asked if I could speak to the doctor, the assistant said she was in surgery and rushed inside. Honestly, do they think patients are fools? You're in a surgery just mins after I walk out and on whom are you performing this imaginery surgery? A while later, she came back and claimed the consultation fee was actually ₹500. It was clear she was just making it up.

I insisted on speaking directly to the doctor. Eventually, Dr. Varsha called me into her office. I asked, “How is your consultation fee ₹500? That’s more than what my gynecologist charges.” She began twisting words, saying things like, “Some people even pay ₹1 lakh for treatment.” But obviously, not everyone pays ₹1 lakh for every illness—that made no sense. I was obviously not going to pay 1100₹ and was asking questions. Then she lost her temper and actually said, “Don’t eat my brain" in those same exact words.

I don’t know what she learned in medical school, but clearly, patience isn’t part of it. Doctors take an oath to serve the needy. The least you can do is take your job seriously and treat patients with dignity. Because of unqualified and careless doctors like this, people suffer—and tragically, sometimes even lose their lives. And they just focus on making money at the expense of innocent/ill people
